column3: “His day” is rendered “the day of his birth.”
The Hebrew has “answered and said”; NASB has “said.”
“A man has been conceived” is rendered “A boy is conceived,” and “I was born” as “I was to be born.”
“Daylight” is rendered “light.”
“Reclaim” is rendered “claim,” and “deep darkness” as “black gloom.” The meaning of “the darkness of day” is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Cursers of a day” is rendered “those … who curse the day”; some read “sea” for “day,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“The eyelids of dawn” is rendered “the breaking dawn.”
“The doors of my womb” is rendered “the opening of my mother's womb.”
“From the womb” is rendered “at birth.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB uses “would have” throughout.
“Rebuilt ruins” is kept; the meaning is uncertain (some read “built monuments”).
Close to the Hebrew.
“Hidden” is rendered “discarded.”
“The weary of strength” is rendered “the weary.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Masters” is rendered “master.”
“Does someone give” is rendered “is light given.”
“Dug” is rendered “dig.”
“The joyful to rejoicing” is rendered “Who rejoice greatly”; some read “to the heap,” and the meaning is uncertain.
NASB repeats “Why is light given” from verse 20; “made inaccessible” is rendered “hedged in.”
“Before my food” is rendered “at the sight of my food.”
“A fear I feared and it came” is rendered as present (“what I fear comes”).
“And turmoil has come” is rendered “but turmoil comes.”
